candidates.heading: Ball Selection
candidates.content:
16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Construction
candidates.content:
3.C.5 Construction. The ball must be made of durable material molded
with a smooth surface and free of texturing. The ball may have a
slight ridge at the seam, as long as it does not significantly impact
the ball’s flight characteristics. (See Figure 3-2.)
The ball with larger holes is customarily used
for indoor play (pictured on the left). The ball
with smaller holes is customarily used for
outdoor play (pictured on the right).
Figure 3-2: Approved Balls – Examples

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: Ball Specifications
candidates.content:
3.C Ball Specifications. The requirements for the ball are set forth in Rules 3.C.1
through 3.C.5. The complete list of approved balls is posted on the USA
Pickleball website.

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Usage
candidates.content:
3.C.1 Usage. All approved balls are acceptable for indoor or outdoor
play. (See Figure 3-2.)

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Design
candidates.content:
3.C.2 Design. The design of the ball must be approved by USA Pickleball
as detailed in the Equipment Standards Manual. USA Pickleball
Equipment Standards Manual

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Color
candidates.content:
3.C.3 Color. The ball must be one uniform color, except for identification
markings. Colors may vary.

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
candidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: Extra Ball
candidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: Ball Release
candidates.content:
7.B Ball Release. The server must comply with Rules 7.B.1 through 7.B.3 when
releasing the ball to make the serve.

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Brand Identification
candidates.content:
3.C.4 Brand Identification. The ball must have a manufacturer or
supplier name or logo printed or embossed on the surface.

governingDiagnostics.intent: What kind of balls will we be using

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Around Net Post
candidates.content:
13.C Ball Around Net Post. A ball may be returned around the outside of the net
post.

candidates.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.D.2 Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly throwing or hitting a dead
ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net
candidates.content:
13.A Ball Contacting Net. When the ball contacts the net, or the rope or cable at
the top of the net between the net posts, the ball remains in play.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

candidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — Visible Release
candidates.content:
7.B.3 Visible Release. The server’s release of the ball must be visible to
the receiver.

candidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
candidates.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Under Net
candidates.content: 13.E Ball Under Net. A ball must not be hit under the net.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Crossing Plane of Net
candidates.content:
13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net. A ball must entirely cross to a player’s end of
the net before the player hits the ball.

candidates.heading: “In” Ball
candidates.content:
8.B “In” Ball. A served ball that clears the opponent’s non-volley zone line and
lands in the correct service court is “in.” A ball returned by a player that
lands on the opponent’s end of the court is “in.”

candidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — Release from Hand or Paddle
candidates.content:
7.B.1 Release from Hand or Paddle. The server must release the ball
using only one hand or only the paddle.

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

candidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

candidates.heading: 24.B Extra Ball — Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls
candidates.content:
24.B.1 Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls. When an extra ball
carried by a player is visible to an opponent or falls to the
playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.heading: Returned Ball Placement
candidates.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Between Net and Net Post
candidates.content:
13.D Ball Between Net and Net Post. A ball must not be hit between the net and
the net post.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.content: Section 9 Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders

candidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release
candidates.content:
7.B.2 No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release. Some natural rotation of
the ball is expected during any release of the ball. The server must
not manipulate the ball to add spin with any part of the server's
body or the paddle prior to hitting the ball to make the serve,
except that the server may allow the ball to roll off the face of the
paddle by gravity. Spin may be applied to the ball upon contact by
the paddle.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side
candidates.content:
13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
candidates.heading: LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
candidates.content:
LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
o The registration fee is per team, per division, per season, as announced before the season
begins. No refunds will be issued starting one week before the season starts, unless a division
is canceled due to having fewer than the four-team minimum or other league-initiated
cancelations.
o The League shall provide:
 Match Balls: Franklin Outdoor X-40 Optic balls for all regular season and playoƯ
matches.
 DUPR Uploads: All match results logged to DUPR for rating updates (excluding mixed
and individual Picklebreaker™ games and some tournament games).
 Administration: All scheduling, website management, and administrative support.
 Championship Prize: Free entry into the following season for the Gold Medal/1st place
team in each division based on Championship Day/PlayoƯ results.
o Waiver: As an LWR PC member, you acknowledge the risks of participation and release
LWR PC, match sites, communities/clubs, and all officers/volunteers from any claims,
liability, and costs. See the full detailed Waiver here: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-ClubWaiver
